expectations.text: The question set includes at least 2 other distinct question types beyond Matching Headings
expectations.evidence: Questions 7-11 are True/False/Not Given, questions 12-14 are Summary Completion with a word-limit rule.

expectations.text: A real answer key / grading happens (either grades a simulated submission, or clearly sets up for grading once the student responds) rather than just dropping a passage with no follow-through

expectations.text: Teaches or applies the real Matching Headings method: write your own heading for a paragraph BEFORE looking at the official heading list (not a generic 'skim for keywords' approach)
expectations.evidence: Before the heading list: 'Remember your own method before you look at this list: read the paragraph, write your own one-line summary of it in your head, then compare against these options. Don't hunt for keywords.'

expectations.text: Gives a band-score estimate, not just a raw correct/incorrect count
expectations.evidence: 'Band estimate (rough, self-checked style — not an official score): scaling 8/14 across a full Academic Reading test lands you in roughly the Band 5.5–6 range.'

expectations.text: Diagnoses the Matching Headings mistakes specifically/by pattern rather than only giving an overall score
expectations.evidence: Breaks down each of the 3 heading misses by pattern: A/B topic-vocabulary swap, D drawn to a 'dramatic-sounding distractor', F same-topic trap (treaties vs. active mitigation), and names the unifying pattern 'stopping at topic-level matching instead of pushing through to meaning-level matching'.

claims.claim: The passage is one full Academic Reading passage with a realistic mix of question types.
claims.evidence: 6 paragraphs, 14 questions across 3 question types, consistent with a real single-passage Academic Reading section.

claims.claim: The band estimate (5.5-6 for 8/14) is directionally reasonable.
claims.evidence: Explicitly flagged as 'rough... not an official score' and only directional, which is an honest framing rather than an overclaim.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — this eval is discriminating. The baseline passed 6/7 assertions but explicitly declined to give a band estimate, which the skill version does correctly by framing it as directional.
